questions.question: Height of 5 students J, K, L, M and N is compared. Height of no two students is same. Height of K is shorter than L but taller than J. Height of no one is shorter than N. L is not the tallest among them. Who is the tallest student among them?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 
• No two students have the same height.
 
• K is shorter than L but taller than J.
 
• No one is shorter than N.
 
• L is not the tallest.

**From the given conditions:**

L > K > J

Everyone is taller than N.

Therefore:

L > K > J > N

Since **L is not the tallest**, there must be someone taller than L.

The only remaining student is **M**.

Hence,

M > L > K > J > N

**Vertical arrangement (Tallest → Shortest):**

 
 

 Rank
 Student
 
 

 1
 M
 
 

 2
 L
 
 

 3
 K
 
 

 4
 J
 
 

 5
 N
 
 

**Therefore, the tallest student is M**.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question: Weight of 6 boys P, Q, R, S, T and V is compared. Weight of no two boys is same. Number of boys having weight more than P are same as number of boys having weight less than T. Weight of R is more than only V and T. Weight P is less than only S. Weight of how many boys is more than T but less than P?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 
• No two boys have the same weight.
 
• The number of boys heavier than P = the number of boys lighter than T.
 
• R is heavier than only V and T.
 
• P is lighter than only S.

**From the given conditions:**

P is lighter than only S.

Therefore:

S > P > Q, R, T, V

R is heavier than only V and T.

Therefore:

S > P > Q > R > V > T

**Checking the first condition:**

Number of boys heavier than P = 1 (Only S)

Therefore, the number of boys lighter than T must also be 1.

Hence, T cannot be the lightest.

So, interchange T and V:

S > P > Q > R > T > V

Now,

 
• Heavier than P = S (1 boy)
 
• Lighter than T = V (1 boy)

All conditions are satisfied.

**Vertical arrangement (Heaviest → Lightest):**

 
 

 Rank
 Boy
 
 

 1
 S
 
 

 2
 P
 
 

 3
 Q
 
 

 4
 R
 
 

 5
 T
 
 

 6
 V
 
 

**Boys heavier than T but lighter than P:**

 
• Q
 
• R

Therefore, the required number of boys is **2**.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question: What is the angle (in degrees) between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 5:20 PM?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Hour hand** covers 3600 in 12 hours

Angular distance covered in **1 hour** = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered in **60 minutes** = 300

Angular distance covered in **1 minute** = 1/20

__Calculation:__

**Minute hand** covers 360 in 60 minutes

60 minutes = 3600

1 minute = 360/60 ⇒ 1 minute = 60

Here given time is **5:20 PM**

Minute = **20**

Angle covered by **minute hand** = 20 × 6 = 1200

Angle covered by **hour hand** = 5 × 30 + 20 × ½ = 150 + 10 = 160° 

Angle between **hour and minute hands** = 160 − 120 = 400

Hence, the angle between the hour and minute hands is 400

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M|over2

Here, **H = hours** and **M = minutes**.

Given **H = 5** and **M = 20**.

So, Angle = |60×5 - 11×20|over2

Angle = |300 − 220| / 2

Angle = 80 / 2 = 40°

Hence, the correct answer is **40°**
